key_insight: Commit contiguous tokens as the Longest Stable Prefix (LSP) during diffusion-language-model decoding to preserve KV-cache locality and avoid costly repeated repairs—yielding much faster, more coherent inference than scattered acceptance.
problem_solved: Diffusion LMs suffer from slow, memory-inefficient inference because 'scattered acceptance' of confident tokens fractures the KV cache, destroys memory locality, and forces repeated corrective passes across unstable boundaries.
method: Detect the Longest Stable Prefix (LSP) across diffusion sampling steps and commit it atomically instead of accepting high-confidence tokens at disjoint positions.
Schedule decoding to maintain contiguous KV-cache state, minimizing cache invalidations and recomputation during subsequent refinement steps.
Implement lightweight checks and heuristics to balance early commit with stability, enabling practical speedups on common hardware.
impact: Preserving KV-cache continuity significantly reduces inference latency and compute for DLMs while improving generated-text coherence—making diffusion-based LMs more practical for real-world, high-throughput deployments.
visual_elements: Side-by-side diagram: 'Scattered acceptance' vs 'LSP commit' showing token acceptance positions and KV-cache fragmentation vs contiguous cache use.
Timeline/flowchart illustrating fewer repair iterations and reduced recomputation when using LSP scheduling.
Bar chart comparing latency, memory transfers, and generation quality (coherence/perplexity) between baseline scattered acceptance and the LSP method.
Memory-heatmap of KV-cache locality before and after LSP to highlight improved hardware utilization.
paper_title: Beyond Scattered Acceptance: Fast and Coherent Inference for DLMs via Longest Stable Prefixes
paper_authors: Pengxiang Li, Joey Tsai, Hongwei Xue, Kunyu Shi, Shilin Yan
